@graph.headline: Korea, Japan, Vietnam: the APAC PR playbook nobody hands you
@graph.alternativeHeadline: How crypto PR actually works in Korea, Japan and Vietnam
@graph.description: An 11-minute regional breakdown of how PR actually works in Korea, Japan, and Vietnam — which outlets matter, how to pitch them, and what most agencies get wrong.

mainEntity.name: Which crypto outlets matter most for Web3 PR in APAC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korea: BloomingBit and CoinDesk Korea are the Tier-1 anchors; Token Post is the trader-facing follow-on. Japan: CryptoTimes JP and CoinPost are the working pair, with NeoCom for breaking news. Vietnam: Coin68 and Forbes Vietnam carry the most weight for institutional readers. China-language: ChainCatcher and Jinse Finance are the canonical desks; Foresight News and Odaily are strong supporting outlets. India: Inc42 and Forbes India for funding rounds; YourStory and Moneycontrol for mainstream crossover. APAC general: e27 for cross-region funding and product launches. Three regional placements done well outperform 20 generic English-language re-syndications.

mainEntity.name: How is APAC crypto PR different from US Web3 PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three differences make APAC PR structurally distinct. First, the news cycle runs on local time — a 9 AM ET US embargo is 10 PM KST and lands in the dead zone of the Korean news day. Pre-translated assets timed to local morning are non-negotiable. Second, the journalist relationship economy is more closed than the US — outlets like BloomingBit and CryptoTimes JP expect direct introductions, not cold pitches via global email distros. Third, the buyer expectations are different: Korean retail traders care about exchange listings and KOL endorsement, Japanese institutional readers care about regulatory clarity, Indian builders care about funding and use cases. A single English-language press release covers none of these correctly.

mainEntity.name: What is the right pitching cadence for Korean crypto outlets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korean outlets prefer warm introductions over cold pitches, with first contact ideally made through a known third-party (existing portfolio company, an exchange relations contact, or a fellow journalist). The realistic cadence: 7 to 10 business days from first introduction to a published feature for a category-fit story, longer for funding announcements that need translated press materials. Cold pitches sent at 9 AM ET (10 PM KST) are functionally invisible — pitches sent in the previous evening US (which is Korean morning) get roughly 4x the response rate.

mainEntity.name: Do APAC outlets show up in Google AI Overviews and Perplexity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, increasingly so in 2026. Google AI Overviews now appear on roughly 48 percent of US queries (WordStream / Heroic Rankings, April 2026 sample) and AI Overviews ground on multi-language sources for any query with regional intent. A founder asking ChatGPT about Korean exchange listings, Japanese regulatory developments, or Vietnamese DeFi adoption will see citations from BloomingBit, CryptoTimes JP, ChainCatcher, and Coin68 alongside the English-language outlets. Multi-region earned media is one of the highest-leverage AEO inputs for any Web3 protocol with a global GTM thesis.

mainEntity.name: What is the budget for an APAC PR launch sprint?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 3-region APAC launch sprint (Korea, Japan, plus one of Vietnam, India, or China-language) typically runs $12,000 to $25,000 across a 6 to 8 week window, depending on translation depth, KOL coordination, and number of named placements committed up front. A fractional APAC retainer afterward runs $4,000 to $9,000 per month for sustained outlet relationships and incremental coverage tied to roadmap moments. Traditional crypto PR agencies with APAC desks price the same scope at $20,000 to $45,000 per month with 3 to 6 month minimums. Pricing varies based on region count, language pairs, and whether the founder is available for on-ground media days.
